question: Who, in the 1860s, undertook a thorough investigation of the gas laws expressing the relationships of pressure, temperature, and volume in carbon dioxide?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thomas Andrews.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thomas Andrews was an Irish chemist who made significant contributions to the study of gases.**
 
• In the 1860s, Andrews conducted a series of experiments on carbon dioxide gas and discovered the critical temperature and pressure of the gas.
 
• He also formulated the concept of the critical point, which is the temperature and pressure at which a gas and liquid are indistinguishable.
 
• Andrews' work on the gas laws of carbon dioxide was an important step towards understanding the behavior of gases in general.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Giulio Natta was an Italian chemist** who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1963 for his work on high polymers.
 
• **John Dalton was an English chemist** who developed the atomic theory of matter and made important contributions to the study of gases.
 
• **Marguerite Perey **was a French physicist who discovered the element francium.
